title: HYDRAA turns to Hyderabad's 160+ stepwells after lakes

slides.head: HYDRAA turns to Hyderabad's 160+ stepwells after lakes
What happened
slides.body: Ranganath announced it at a stepwell awareness programme in Hyderabad, where Akarma Foundation showed an exhibition on Telangana's water legacy.

slides.head: Why it matters
slides.body: He linked it to the El Nino water crisis: stepwells are more decentralised than lakes and restoring them should help the groundwater table.

slides.head: stepwells in Hyderabad
slides.body: Telangana has 600+ stepwells, and Ranganath says the real count is likely much higher.

slides.head: Dig deeper
slides.body: Telangana has more than 600 stepwells, HYDRAA's chief said, and the number is likely higher.

slides.head: What to watch
slides.body: What comes out of Tuesday's meeting with the Union Home Secretary on water, floods and drought. Ask: How many of Hyderabad's stepwells still hold water today?

slides.head: Spill the tea, daily
slides.body: Hyderabad news in 30 seconds, with the numbers and the questions. Follow for tomorrow's drop: spillthetea.news

captions.instagram:
HYDRAA turns to Hyderabad's 160+ stepwells after lakes

HYDRAA Commissioner A. Ranganath said the SOPs written for lake conservation will now be used to restore stepwells in Telangana, and the idea may go national.

Why it matters: He linked it to the El Nino water crisis: stepwells are more decentralised than lakes and restoring them should help the groundwater table.

Source: The Hindu. Image: The Hindu
